title: fix(getEnvironment): share the account-name lookup across processes; back off on TooManyRequests
description:
## .what

`getEnvironment()` throttles under parallel jest: `getEnvAccessFromAwsAccountName` calls `GetAccountInformation` once per cold module registry, and the aws Account API refuses the burst with `TooManyRequestsException`.

## .measured — 2026-11-16, ahbode/svc-chat integration suite on a 36-core grove

- run 1: 176 passed, 9 failed. run 2: 178 passed, 7 failed — a DIFFERENT set each run
- every failure: `TooManyRequestsException: Too Many Requests` at `getEnvAccessFromAwsAccountName.ts:56`, via `getEnvironment.ts:131` and `:183`
- the same suite is green on a 4-core grove. jest runs ~cores-1 workers, so 36 cores ⇒ ~35 cold lookups at once
- the identity is fine: 176+ tests reach aws through it

## .why the extant cache does not help

`getEnvironment.ts:106` caches in a module-level `simple-in-memory-cache`. jest gives each test FILE its own module registry, in its own worker process, so the cache is shared within one file only — ~29 files ⇒ ~29 cold `GetAccountInformation` calls, most of them concurrent.

## .the shape of the fix

1. a cross-process cache for the account-name read: a file on disk keyed by the caller identity (account + role arn from sts), short ttl, atomic write. one process asks aws; the rest read the file. it serves any multi-process caller, not jest alone
2. retry with backoff + jitter on `TooManyRequestsException` (or `retryMode: 'adaptive'` on the `AccountClient`) — a safety net, since the first cold burst still happens

clamp: a test that fires N concurrent cold `getEnvironment()` calls across processes and asserts ONE `GetAccountInformation` reaches the client.

## .who waits on it

the hetzner camp grove smoketest (dev-env-setup, `git.grove.provision test`) stays red on this alone; every other rung holds.
